messages:
alex: heads-up — started seeing intermittent OOMs on shared-gpu-7 when co-hosting tiny-gpt and llama-13b-v2 after the kernel-selection tweak landed. behavior is weird: happens under medium concurrency, not at peak.

maria: ugh. did it start after the kernel-selector change yesterday? any repro steps?

alex: yes, rolled the selector change at 18:12 UTC. repro: run mixed traffic (50/50) with batching window=8, kv_cache enabled. here's a short profile from the failing run:

```
[perf] timeline summary
0.00s  init workspace alloc  1.2GiB
0.11s  kernel A (attn)         0.9GiB
0.32s  kernel B (fwd)          2.6GiB  <-- spike before eviction
0.35s  kvcache promote         0.8GiB
0.36s  OOM: cudaMalloc failed  (out of memory)

active_buffers: [modelA_kv: 1.1GiB, modelB_kv: 2.0GiB, workspace: 1.5GiB]
allocator state: slab small-frag 18% free, pinned_slices: 3
```

alex: note: when forcing kernel B (older kernel) the spike doesn't show. suspecting kernel-specific workspace/temporary buffer sizing changed.

cheng: can you paste the kernel-selector log for that request? i'd like to see why the fallback chose the new kernel. also pinging @sam for allocator insights.

alex: sure — snippet below (selector decided based on sequence-length distribution and opt_cost):

```
[selector] model=llama-13b-v2 seq=153 opt=A (new_kernel) cost_delta=+12%
[selector] cache_compat=true, quant_profile=nvf8
[executor] pinned to stream 3, work_sz_hint=2.6GiB
```

sam: hmm work_sz_hint 2.6GiB looks high for that seq. new kernel probably requests larger temp buffers (partial gemm workspace). did kernel change include a larger tiled buffer?

priya: FYI i saw a perf regression on L13B in canary yesterday, linked to the kernel refactor PR #1482. believed to improve latency but might increase temp mem.

maria: if true, should we make selector consider peak_temp_alloc in cost model so it avoids kernels that would breach slack on multi-model nodes?

cheng: +1. short-term mitigation: add a conservative slack margin when scheduling co-resident models. can we also prefer kernel variants with smaller peak working set when kvcache pressure is high?

alex: tried an experiment: forced kernel selection to old_kernel for llama and enabled 'workspace_reuse=v2' optimizer. OOMs stopped. throughput dropped ~3% but stable.

sam: good data point. can you capture allocator free list fragmentation before/after? we need to know if temp allocations cause slice starvation.

alex: frag snapshot attached below: (copied)

```
allocator.free_slices: 12
largest_free_slice: 256MiB
total_free: 2.8GiB
fragmentation_ratio: 0.42
pinned_slices: [0x7f8.., 0x8c2..] (3 pinned, total 1.1GiB)
```

priya: pinned_slices are likely kvcache-reserved segments. when kernel spikes, it triggers new large malloc that can't be satisfied causing eviction attempts; eviction blocks due to pinned pages.

maria: short checklist: 1) revert kernel refactor on selector (rollback flag) 2) add kernel peak_mem estimate to selector heuristics 3) adjust kvcache eviction to preempt temp workspace when safe 4) add e2e test for mixed-hosting with seq diversity.

cheng: i'll open a small PR to surface peak_temp_estimate in the model profile metadata. alex can you collect per-kernel temp histograms (use --dump-kernel-stats)?

alex: running dumps now, will push artifacts to buildkite. also can reproduce with a deterministic script: `scripts/repro/multi_model_swap_test --a tiny-gpt --b llama-13b-v2 --concurrency 12 --batch-window 8 --kv=on`

deploy-bot: deploy queued for selector-hotfix branch to canary-cluster at 19:03 UTC :rocket:

ops-bot: note: node shared-gpu-7 has SATURATION=0.62, memory_pressure=0.78. auto-oom-kill is disabled for canary.

sam: action items: (1) alex collect kernel histograms and attach; (2) cheng add peak_temp to model profiles; (3) priya try soft-evict kvcache earlier when workspace request > threshold; (4) maria enable selector rollback flag on canary if OOMs persist.

maria: +1 on action items. can we keep the thread for quick status updates? i'll run the canary watch for the next 2 hours.

alex: uploaded artifacts: buildkite.com/redwood/infer/12345/artifacts/1943214321/kernel_stats.tgz

cheng: PR opened: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1567 — adds peak_temp_estimate field and disables kernels with >20% extra peak on multi-model nodes by default.

priya: implementing soft-evict now. quick note: need to ensure evict doesn't thrash the kvcache for hot prefixes — adding threshold by prefix_age + prefix_hits.

sam: thanks all. if we can get selector to incorporate peak_temp and add the reclaimed workspace path (reuse buffer chain), i think this will solve most of the instability without full rollback.

alex: will update with post-fix perf numbers in a few hours. thanks for the quick triage :thumbsup:
